items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-06-15
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well, who was the best trombone player then, Norfolk?

ctx.x: It's not just you who says that. I don't like to play that part of the world. See, they can do all they want, but I feel like I get along better. See, I don't worry about the other part of what he's doing. Let them worry about what I'm doing. You see, because I can get off. I can ruin myself and get off in front of the pattern of you and do what you're doing. When I look at it, I'm going to be doing nothing. Understand? So if I'm doing like I've been doing and do it to my best of knowledge just before they keep…
Well, who was the best trombone player then, Norfolk?

A real thunk trombone player, you know what I mean? Well, I tell you, at the time then, you see Dick, tell you the truth, them was more of a musical man, but good man, you understand? And they could play jazz too, you understand? But there was more musical man, you know? India was always good trombone players. Now they had to take like, they had Boris Fletcher right around there playing trombone. They had George Washington, Eddie Morris. Now all the people was playing more trombone when I was playing. They were…
